subject: MAP: Staged reserve & acceptance sprint for EdgeHealth capacity
body:
From: Samir Patel <samir@edgehealth.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina@edgehealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity needs / MAP kickoff: EdgeHealth pilot

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning — really appreciated the walkthrough. As discussed, we'd like to formalize a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for the pilot so procurement has something concrete to review. Top-level asks from our side:
- Target go-live for pilot: mid-November (approx. 8 weeks)
- Baseline throughput target: 150 QPS on chat generation (95th pct latency under 300ms)
- Data residency: US-only; SOC2 evidence required in procurement package
- Prefer a staged reservation approach (initial tranche + 2-week canary)

Can you share a MAP that maps evaluation criteria to procurement milestones and proposed GPU pool sizing with lead times? Procurement will need an estimate for reserved capacity and a proposed acceptance checklist (smoke tests + performance gates).

Samir
EdgeHealth — VP Product

---

On Tue, Sep 22, 2026 at 11:30 AM Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai> wrote:

> From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
> To: Samir Patel <samir@edgehealth.ai>
> Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lina Gomez <lina@edgehealth.ai>
> Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -0700
> Subject: RE: Capacity needs / MAP kickoff: EdgeHealth pilot
>
> Hi Samir — thanks, this is helpful. Attached is a first-pass MAP draft and a stove-piped GPU sizing estimate for the pilot (attached files). High level proposal (summary):
>
> 1) MAP milestones (8-week timeline)
>    - Week 0: MAP sign + PO intent (procurement receives proposal)
>    - Week 1–2: Eval sprint (integration + 1k prompts test harness)
>    - Week 3: Performance baseline & QC (tokenization/latency profiles)
>    - Week 4: Procurement finalize reservation tranche 1 (50% of target pool)
>    - Week 5: Hardware delivery & staging onboarding (private VPC)
>    - Week 6: Canary (2-week reduced-traffic acceptance window)
>    - Week 8: Full ramp to committed throughput
>
> 2) Sizing assumptions (proposal)
>    - Target pool: 8x A800-equivalent GPUs (mixed 80% FP16 low-latency serving + 20% heavier batches)
>    - Cold-start KV sizing to sustain 150 QPS at target latency (prefetch + prefix cache)
>    - Fallback plan: reduced-capacity variant (quantized 4-bit) to handle peak spikes
>
> 3) Procurement asks / artifacts
>    - SOC2 report + data flow diagram (we'll add to the shared Drive link)
>    - PO template + initial invoice schedule (30/60/90)
>    - DocuSign-friendly MAP acceptance checklist (smoke, perf, infra hardening)
>
> I'm looping in Marissa on procurement cadence and Karthik for the technical lead-time details. If that timeline looks feasible to you, we can convert the attached MAP into a mutual action document for signatures and a HubSpot milestone.
>
> Next steps: Samir — confirm the acceptance gates (smoke/perf) and whether you want the canary to run on production traffic (we recommend a sampled production feed during canary). We'll hold the initial tranche until PO payment terms are agreed.
>
> Thanks,
> Sean
> Senior Solutions Director
> Redwood Inference
>
> Attachment: EdgeHealth_MAP_Draft_v3.pdf
> Attachment: GPU_sizing_estimate.xlsx

>

> >
> > Hi team — adding procurement-level milestones and risks. A few notes from the procurement/readiness perspective:
> >
> > - Procurement will need a clear cancellation/scale-down policy in the MAP (we typically propose 30-day notice windows for tranche reductions).
> > - For staged reservation: propose Tranche 1 = 50% commit (8-week term), Tranche 2 = additional 30% (optional), Holding buffer = 20% (on-demand burst).
> > - Lead times: hardware allocation and private deployment onboarding typically require 3–5 weeks after PO (region dependent). Add contingency for custom networking (VPC peer) + security review (SOC2 evidence).
> > - Finance ask: initial 50% deposit on tranche 1 to lock capacity; remainder on successful canary acceptance.
> >
> > I've attached a procurement checklist in the Drive link and flagged the acceptance items that map to vendor invoices. If procurement wants a tighter lead time, we can explore a Dedicated express window (higher unit cost) to shorten the 3–5 week delivery.
> >
> > Marissa
> > Head of Customer Onboarding
> > Redwood Inference

> > >
> > > Hi all — adding technical sizing + lead-time clarity. A few concrete items to include in the MAP so the acceptance gates are unambiguous:
> > >
> > > - GPU type & perf: target 8x A800-equivalent (or 6x H100 if heavy parallelism needed); A800 gives better latency cost balance for chat workloads.
> > > - Sequence length profile: we need a sample set (>5000 queries) from EdgeHealth to finalize cache footprint and batch sizing.
> > > - Quantization plan: baseline run on FP16; fallback to 4-bit quantized model during peak to keep SLOs. We should include test cases showing +/- delta in hallucination rates for quantized runs.
> > > - Lead times: procurement PO -> resource ready is ~3 weeks if using standard pool; 1–2 week acceleration if customer opts for express allocation (higher cost).
> > > - Canary definition: 14-day window, 10% production traffic sampling, perf gates: 95th latency < 320ms and error rate <0.5%.
> > >
> > > I'll contribute a short tech appendix to the MAP that lists perf tests and the specific smoke-test harness we'll run (load shape, burn-in, KV-cache warmup steps).
> > >
> > > Karthik
> > > Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

> > > > - Canary staffing: recommend 24/7 on-call for the 14-day canary (rotate ops + SE).
> > > > - Canary rollback plan: pre-defined fallback model (quantized variant) + regional fallback to hosted API if private pool degraded.
> > > > - Acceptance artefacts: final perf report, SOC2 evidence, and signed MAP + PO.
